newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks extend powerful rally.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks extend powerful rally.

text.p: Wall Street stocks staged a powerful rally Tuesday as falling interest rates, coupled with mounting optimism about corporate profits, produced more record highs on a host of major indices.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 53.11 points at 6,762.29, its fourth straight record finish and sixth high of the year.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,800 to 802 on heavy volume of 531 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite, Standard & Poor's composite and the NYSE Composite indices also set new highs.
Stocks got an early boost when key economic indicators for December confirmed inflation remains at bay.

The Consumer Price Index's "core" rate, which excludes food and energy costs, rose only 0.1 percent, triggering a big rally in bonds that sent interest rates falling and gave stock traders a green light to buy.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond gained a full point, cutting its yield to 6.77 percent from 6.85 percent at Monday's close.
"We had lot of reports today but most traders were hanging their hats on the CPI," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital.
The news boosted the stocks of banks and other financial companies. J.P. Morgan & Co. rose two points to 104-1/2 and Citicorp jumped 3-3/4 to 104-1/4.

Interest rates aside, the day clearly belonged to technology stocks, particularly personal computer makers. International Business Machines Corp. rose 2-7/8 to 166-3/4 and Gateway 2000 Inc. surged four to 56.
"We had an across-the-board run on technology stocks," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers.

"There is a personal computer upgrade cycle going on in the corporate world and everyone is looking for a very good number out of Intel," he said, referring to Intel Corp.'s plans to release its quarterly earnings after the close.

Intel did not disappoint, reporting fourth-quarter earnings of $2.13 per share, more than doubling the 98 cents per share it earned in the year-ago period. The results also exceeded Wall Street estimates, which averaged $1.84 per share.
The sheer strength of Intel's report led analysts to believe the rally by technology stocks could be far from over.

In surpassing Wall Street's estimates, Intel set the stage for an extended sector rally, said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "Today could just be the tip of the iceberg for techs."
Intel, which also declared a two-for-one stock split, rose 1/4 to 147-1/8 prior to the company's earnings announcement.
Bucking the bullish trend were the shares of health maintenance organisations, which slipped on fears that the United States would move to slow the growth rate of their premiums.
Oxford Health Plans Inc. fell 2-3/4 to 52-5/8 and United Healthcare Corp. lost 3/4 to 43-5/8.

Among individual issues, Payless ShoeSource Inc. jumped 2-3/8 to 37 after announcing it would acquire J. Baker Inc.'s Parade of Shoes unit for undisclosed terms. Payless also said it planned to buy back up to $150 million in stock, representing about 11 percent of its shares outstanding.
J. Baker rose 13/16 to 6-7/8.
Netscape Communications Corp. skidded 4-1/2 to 42-1/4 after Merrill Lynch expressed caution about the company's outlook.
The Nasdaq Composite index jumped 15.45 points to 1,346.36, a new high.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 9.35 to 768.86, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.22 to 588.35.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 4.36 to 405.07, a new high. The average share was up 45 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,438,119, up 78.073, or 1.06 percent.
